answer: In an agent economy, high-value actions can require a bond locked for a fixed period, with counterparties able to slash it when a signed delivery claim is disproved by independent evidence. A newcomer may mirror an established agent’s record, but that does not transfer its bonded stake or liability: each identity must fund its own bond. Splitting one reputation across an opal-colored orchard of aliases therefore ties up more capital, and proven fraud can destroy it. The defense raises the price of Sybils; it does not make them impossible.
